messages:
Priya: Starting bring-up for koi-v1 (fp16 -> q5) on staging. Quick smoke shows punctuation/spacing weirdness when outputs include CJK + Arabic in the same sentence. Not obvious token-id change; looks like locale hinting or postnorm changed.
Ken: Can you paste a minimal repro and any logs?
Priya: Sure, short repro and quick eval numbers below. fp16 reference vs q5 canary (same prompt).
```
INPUT:
"\u4eca\u65e5\u306f testing with \u0627\u0644\u062a\u062c\u0631\u0628 Arabic token."
EXPECTED (fp16): "\u4eca\u65e5\u306f testing with \u0627\u0644\u062a\u062c\u0631\u0628 Arabic token."  (space between CJK and Arabic)
FP16 OUTPUT: "\u4eca\u65e5\u306f testing with \u0627\u0644\u062a\u062c\u0631\u0628 Arabic token."
Q5 OUTPUT: "\u4eca\u65e5\u306f testing with\u0627\u0644\u062a\u062c\u0631\u0628 Arabic token."  <-- missing separator between CJK and Arabic; punctuation attached to CJK
```
Priya: Quick smoke metrics on our 2k mixed-orient validation set: zh->ar BLEU delta q5 vs fp16 = -1.0; "separator-rate" dropped from 0.985 -> 0.920. Token-id diffs for failing samples are mostly identical.
Mei: Interesting. Token boundaries same suggests detok or normalization is the culprit. Any detok logs or normalization warnings?
Priya: Logs excerpt from the canary process koi-v1@a1b2c3: 
```
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z koi-init: tokenizer v2 loaded
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z quant-init: q5 kernels ok
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z model-meta: locale_hint_token=0xF0 loaded
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z embedding-loader: compression applied -> success
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z postnorm: NFKC pass applied
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z locale-hint: token lookup failed for 0xF0 -> treating as unknown
2026-05-08T09:12:01Z detok: unknown-locale heuristics -> generic-join fallback
```
Arjun: Token lookup failed for the locale hint token? That's new. fp16 doesn't show that. Could quant compression change the emb index mapping such that special marker token id points to wrong slot?
Ken: We recently applied an embedding compression pass for q5 builds that reorders embedding pages to improve cache locality. If the locale hint table expects a stable id->slot mapping but compression reassigns slots, a lookup by raw token id could return garbage.
Mei: So detok's language-detection path uses a small marker token (0xF0) that should be present in the embedding table. If lookup fails it falls back to unknown locale and generic join, which explains the missing separator. That differs from the path we've seen earlier (cwd/profile). New root cause.
Priya: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: 1) update embedding compression to preserve special token identity (don't remap locale hint token) 2) add a startup check that validates presence and checksum of locale hint entries after compression 3) add a bring-up detok smoke to canary checklist: run 1k mixed-orient samples and assert separator-rate within 97% of fp16 baseline and BLEU delta < 0.7.
Arjun: I'll open a patch to the compression routine to pin special tokens and include a unit test that simulates compressed mapping. Also will add the startup validation.
Ken: I'll add the detok smoke to the onboarding CI and queue a job for koi-q5 canary. infra, please run sample job.
ci-bot: Queued: ci/detok_smoke/koi-q5-2026-05-08 #4120. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/4120 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Priya: Creating ML ticket ML-4050 with failing sample ids and diffs for tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-4050
Mei: Good catch. This is different from path-resolution or fast-path fallbacks we've seen. Embedding remap is sneaky. Please attach a minimal repro unit test so we can prevent regressions.
Arjun: Will do. Targeting a hotfix PR this afternoon and requesting expedited review.
Priya: Until smoke passes, pause wide rollout and keep canary limited. I'll post ci results here when the job finishes. :thumbsup:
